what: Within-family reseed test, 2026-09-25: does each family generator yield a new accepted instance for a new world seed, does the key still hold, and is the new instance a different examination point or the same one with new numbers?
how: fam_s/gen_s.py and fam_v/gen_v.py take a seed; fam_b/gen_b.py and fam_d/gen_ds.py hard-code world seed 0, so they were reseeded with harness/reseed.py and harness/fast_ds.py (the latter only parallelises the per-reading answer sweep over 4 processes). Every accepted instance was then re-solved by its own reference solver, graded by its own verifier, and put through the family self-check, the audit gates A1-A5 and the leakage gate.

generator_rejected.3: G8 mechanism inferability: skipping the deduction does not move the key by more than 10x tol

audit_gates.1: FAIL A1 threshold margin: decision d03 flips within 1x tol of its own threshold

B_bounds.finding: the audit gates are not in the generator's accept loop - gen_b accepted an instance the corpus audit rejects

generator_rejected.1: G12 band width of one suite not shown by >=2 log rows
generator_rejected.3: G11 the exact-value inversion gets no values item wrong

V_falsify.finding: the seed only drives the certification fuzzing; family V is a single hand-authored instance

O_pack.note: seed changes packer parameters and the test suite; the specification code pack_ref.py is fixed. Not re-run here (calibration exceeds the per-call process limit).

conclusion: Within a family, new instances are cheap (seconds to half a minute), accurate (reference 1, self-checks and gates pass) and filtered by gates (end-to-end yield S 3/3, B 1/3, D-sealed 1/6). But every accepted reseed has the same instruction text and the same item structure as the shipped instance: it is the same examination point with new numbers, i.e. the parameter-level variation the user ruled out as a new question. Whether the difficulty of D-sealed and S transfers to reseeds has not been measured on models.
